CHOICE: 2
CONFIDENCE: 3

Solution 1 is wrong at k=1. A single candidate b cannot α-dominate every outsider for any α > 0 when m → ∞, because some outsider is preferred to b by more than (1−α)n voters with probability tending to 1. Solution 1's answer k/(k+1) gives 1/2 at k=1, so it fails.

Solution 3 relies on a heuristic scaling claim (P(p ≤ u) ~ u^{n/t}) that is not justified. Its answer 1 − 1/k tends to 1 as k grows, which I could not reconcile with my rough checks for k=2. The designs I tried at σ = 0.55 all gave outsider cost well below 1.

Solution 2 sets up a large-deviation reduction and gives an explicit optimization argument with a convexity bound, so its reasoning is more checkable. It gives 0 at k=1 and 1/4 at k=2. I did not fully verify its optimality, so my confidence is moderate.
